extracted.intended_audience: R package authors and prospective reviewers participating in rOpenSci's software peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting, reviewing, and editing R packages through rOpenSci's open software peer-review process; covers expectations for authors, reviewers, editorial roles, and available templates/resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: All the packages contributed by community members go through a process of open peer review to ensure a consistent level of quality for our users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is open (transparent) and allows discussion where exceptions are requested; review conversation happens publicly (issues/PRs) so reviewers and authors can discuss changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: useful feedback and improving software quality
rubrics_metrics.description: We hope you submit your package for review because you value the feedback. We aim to provide useful feedback to package authors and for our review process to be open, non-adversarial, and focused on improving software quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be constructive and targeted at improving the package (code, documentation, maintenance), not adversarial criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors retain ownership and control
rubrics_metrics.description: You’ll retain ownership and control of your package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rOpenSci offers support (ongoing maintenance help, updates to R/dependencies, CRAN policy issues) but does not assume ownership; authors remain responsible for their packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packages must meet rOpenSci guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process ensures that your package meets our guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should read the 'guide for authors' before opening a submission issue; adherence to the documented guidelines is expected and is the basis for review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Our code of conduct is mandatory for everyone involved in our review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants (authors, reviewers, editors) must follow the code of conduct; this governs acceptable behaviour and community interactions during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic documentation website and CI/deployment benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages in our suite get a documentation website that is automatically built and deployed after each push.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission to rOpenSci carries infrastructural benefits (automatic docs builds); package authors should expect and use these resources as part of the package maintenance workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and cross-listing benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci will promote your package through our webpage, blog, and social media. rOpenSci packages can be cross-listed with other repositories such as CRAN and BioConductor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may gain visibility and discoverability; packages that include a short accompanying paper can be fast-tracked to the Journal of Open-Source Software after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure: read guides and open a submission issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to submit a package, read our guide for authors before opening a submission issue in this repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions in the guide for authors and use the provided templates (review template, editor’s template, review request template) to prepare and request review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility and volunteering
rubrics_metrics.description: To volunteer to be one of our reviewers, please fill out this short form providing your contact information and areas or expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rOpenSci is always looking for reviewers with both general package-writing experience and domain expertise in the fields packages are used for; volunteering requires declaring expertise to match reviews appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review as a two-way conversation and learning opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is a two-way conversation. By reviewing packages, you’ll have the chance to continue to learn development practices from authors and other reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should engage collaboratively; the process is intended to be educational and network-building as well as evaluative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of templates and supplementary resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository and gitbook include different templates: review template, editor’s template, review request template, and other resources (guide for editors, policies, maintenance chapters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors, reviewers, and editors should use the provided templates to standardize submissions and reviews; the gitbook contains more detailed practices for development, maintenance, and peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial governance and rotating Editor-in-Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci’s Software Peer Review process is run by a team of dedicated editors and reviewers. We rotate our Editor-in-Chief, generally every three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a defined editorial team and governance; authors and reviewers interact with editors who mediate the review and maintain process continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative process and invitation to provide feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Our review process is always in development, and we encourage feedback and discussion on how to improve the process on our forum and in the ropensci/software-review-meta issue tracker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are encouraged to suggest improvements to the review workflow and policies via public channels; the process evolves with community input.
